steps.body: Each tenth can be split into 10 smaller parts. That makes 100 equal cells — each one is a hundredth of the whole.
steps.narration: Each tenth can be split into 10 smaller parts. That makes 100 equal cells — each one is a hundredth of the whole.

widget.prompt: Shade the grid to show 0.10. Each full column is one tenth; each cell is one hundredth.

commonCounts.feedback: That shades one single cell — one hundredth. One full COLUMN is ten cells, because a tenth splits into ten hundredths.

widget.successFeedback: One full column — 10 hundredths, which is exactly one tenth: 0.10 and 0.1 name the same amount.
widget.lowFeedback: The shaded amount is still below the target. Fill whole columns for the tenths digit first, then single cells for the hundredths.
widget.highFeedback: The shaded amount has gone past the target. Each full column is one tenth — check the tenths digit before adding single cells.

predict.prompt: The square now has 100 cells, in 10 columns of 10. How many cells make one full column?
predict.reveal: A column holds 10 of the 100 cells. One tenth of the square equals ten hundredths of it.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g4d hundredths intro.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for g4d hundredths intro must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines g4d hundredths intro.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: Each cell is one hundredth, so 4 cells writes as 0.04.

widget.prompt: A unit square is split into 100 equal cells, and 4 of them are shaded. Write the shaded amount as a decimal.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the count of shaded cells, and a count of parts is a whole number. Each cell is one hundredth of the square, so the count belongs after the decimal point, ending in the hundredths place.
That reads the count as tenths, but each cell is one hundredth of the square — a tenth is a whole column of 10 cells. Write the count so it ends in the hundredths place.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Each cell is one hundredth. Write the count of shaded cells so its last digit lands in the hundredths place — two places after the decimal point.

0.30 is 30 hundredths, so 30 cells must be shaded.

widget.prompt: A hundredths grid has 100 equal cells. How many cells must be shaded to show 0.30?

commonErrors.feedback: That shades only the tenths digit's worth of single cells. In 0.30 the 3 sits in the tenths place, so it is worth 3 full columns — 30 cells — before the hundredths digit adds any more.
That count is one full column — ten cells — past the amount. The tenths digit of 0.30 calls for exactly 3 full columns.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Each full column of the grid is one tenth — ten cells — and each single cell is one hundredth. Turn each digit of the decimal into cells and add the two counts.
